subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should the disabled-heartbeat-delivery diagnostic keep the shipped `reason: "target-none"` and add a human-facing hint/status message, or should the machine reason be renamed?
rationale: The current reason is already present in tests and the latest release, so the user-facing fix is small but the event contract shape needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Add hint and keep reason
options.body: Keep `target-none` as the machine reason, add an optional configuration-disabled hint, and surface it in CLI/status output.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting a compatibility break for parsers of heartbeat event reasons.

options.title: Keep current diagnostics
options.body: Leave the shipped event and status output unchanged and accept the current support/debugging confusion.

recommendation.title: Add hint and keep reason
recommendation.body: Keep `target-none` as the machine reason, add an optional configuration-disabled hint, and surface it in CLI/status output.

likelyOwner.reason: The default `target: none` behavior appears to come from the merged default-routing PR, so this is the closest history-backed owner for the contract choice.
